author: Linnaeus, 1758
summary: 주로 동해안에서 겨울을 나는 드문 겨울철새로, 암초가 많은 바닷가에서 작은 무리를 지어 지낸다. 잠수해 갑각류와 조개류를 잡아먹고, 쉴 때는 해안 바위에 올라간다. 시베리아 동부, 캄차카, 알래스카에서 북아메리카 서북부 해안, 쿠릴열도 북부, 그린란드 남부, 아이슬란드, 아메리카 동북 연안에 걸쳐 번식하며, 겨울에는 번식지 아래쪽 지역으로 내려와 지낸다.

art.subject: Harlequin Duck (Histrionicus histrionicus), adult male in winter, as seen on rocky East Sea coasts from November to March: plumage dark slate-blue with a faint metallic sheen; a large white crescent in front of the eye from the bill base up onto the forehead, continuing as a narrow chestnut stripe along the side of the black crown; a round white spot on the ear coverts and a vertical white stripe on the side of the neck; a narrow white collar line and a white vertical bar on each side of the breast, all edged black; white stripes along the scapulars and tertials; flanks rich chestnut; tail dark. Bill small and short, bluish-grey; iris dark; legs grey.
art.pose: resting on a wave-washed coastal rock
art.scene: Korean winter East Sea coast with dark reefs and breaking surf; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view standing on a rock: slate-blue body, white crescent before the eye, chestnut crown-side stripe, round white ear spot, white neck stripe, black-edged white collar and breast bar, chestnut flanks, small bluish-grey bill
adult female, side view swimming: dark sooty-brown overall, white patch on the lores in front of the eye, round white spot on the ear coverts, paler belly, small dark bill
art.build: Small, compact sea duck, about 43cm, smaller and rounder than a Mallard. Steep forehead, rounded head and a very small, short, stubby bill much shorter than the head. Rides high and buoyant in surf, diving among breaking waves, and hauls out on wave-washed rocks. Legs short, grey, set far back. At rest the wingtips reach the base of the tail. Tail rather long, pointed and dark, often raised. Flies fast and low over the sea; the wings are dark without any white panel.
avoid: Do not paint a long or broad duck bill; it is tiny and stubby below a steep forehead.
Do not paint the male bright blue or black; he is dark slate-blue.
Do not add white wing patches or a white speculum.
Do not move the male's chestnut onto the breast; the chestnut is on the flanks and the crown sides only.
